limits_note: Per-object-cap 5 GB / 50 GB per record; moderation gate ('Once you submit your record for publication it will be reviewed by the Materials Cloud moderators'), scope-gated to computational materials science, and moderators explicitly police 'excessive submission rate'.
reliability_note: EPFL-hosted and stable, but moderation is substantive (refereeable-quality requirement) and rate-policed. The opposite of an anonymous dump. Data survives; throughput is editorially throttled.

extras.quota_verbatim: Per-record, not per-account: '5 GB for general materials science research data, 50 GB for AiiDA databases. For larger datasets please contact us.' Records are unlimited and each gets a DOI, so this is a per-record-unlimited pattern rather than a 500 GB single-shot store.
extras.limits_verbatim: Per-object-cap 5 GB / 50 GB per record; moderation gate ('Once you submit your record for publication it will be reviewed by the Materials Cloud moderators'), scope-gated to computational materials science, and moderators explicitly police 'excessive submission rate'.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free, and unusually well-instrumented: 'Access to metadata and data files is provided over standard protocols such as HTTP and OAI-PMH.' No metering. Probe: GET /record/2026.196 -> 200, 90,945 bytes of record page.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Unlimited records x 5 GB (or 50 GB for AiiDA databases). 100 records at 5 GB = 500 GB; the 50 GB AiiDA tier halves that to 10 records.
extras.tooling_verbatim: Email self-registration with a personal work area; HTTP + OAI-PMH read; DOI minting per record; versioning of published records. AiiDA provenance integration is the native client for the 50 GB tier.
extras.agent_focus: Exotic and institutional surfaces: national libraries/archives, museum and heritage platforms, genomics/biobank consortia, audiovisual archives, government open-data portals, institutional repositories (DSpace/EPrints/Dataverse/Invenio) that accept EXTERNAL depositors, publishing platforms, religious/cultural bulk corpora. Priority seam: a university or national repository whose deposit door is open to anyone and whose write path is an API.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
